result.title: Multimodal View Training: Learning More Through Different Modalities
result.summary: Can a language model learn more from the same information simply by encountering it in different forms? We answer this in the affirmative by introducing Multimodal View Training (MVT), a simple training approach that presents identical information through text, speech, and images, without requiring new facts or supervision. Starting from a text sample, MVT generates corresponding audio and rendered-text image views, and trains a multimodal language model to produce the same target output across all three views. To further bring these benefits to text-only large language models (LLMs), we train lightweight connector modules to pretrained audio and vision encoders, allowing the LLM to learn from multimodal inputs while retaining its text-only architecture at inference. Across question answering, machine unlearning, and knowledge editing, adaptive MVT improves QA recall by +15.2 percentage points, forget quality by +40.7 points, and editing generality by +25.2 points over text-only training. Combining MVT with standard augmentation further improves QA and editing generality. Our theoretical analysis illustrates how training across modalities can shift weight updates toward shared factual content and reduce their reliance on features specific to each view.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Multimodal View Training：把同一文本样本渲染成语音与文字图像视图，训练多模态语言模型对三种视图输出相同目标，并用轻量 connector 让纯文本 LLM 在训练时接收多模态输入、推理时保持文本架构；在问答、机器遗忘与知识编辑上报告了提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「跨视图共享事实内容、弱化视图特有特征」的训练思路，可供核查视觉旁路是否只在编码层面起作用、以及对 VLM 内部事实性表示与模态不变性的影响；但不涉及推理期 latent 状态生成或证据筛选，与 LVR 主线仅有训练监督层面的借鉴线索。
